⏳ **F-2608-1 — RT-01's STEP-1 PRECONDITION IS AN OWNER-HELD FILE THAT NO FIRE HAS EVER CHECKED, AND ITS ABSENCE IS A *STOP WITH A DESK LINE* FOUR DAYS FROM A DATED TRIGGER — MEASURED PRESENT, BANKED AS A NEGATIVE (fire s2608, dry board, 76th consecutive; CODEX-WALL standing, owner POLICY, read AT SOURCE).** F-2595-1's own lesson is that a dated duty *"accumulates verified facts and unverified verbs, and the verbs are what a fire actually executes on the day"* — so when a trigger approaches, TYPE THE STEPS. Three fires have now pre-flighted RT-01 (s2594 the mint's argv shape, s2595 the phantom baseline, s2597 the fence shape and its four consumers), and **not one of them checked whether the thing step 1 reads actually exists.** RT-01's first verb is `node scripts/rotation-mint.mjs --week <YYYY-Www> --salt-file ~/.goldrush/rotation-salt --append …`, and the duty's own closing sentence rules that *"a missing salt file is a STOP with one desk line, never a default"* — i.e. an ABSENT salt does not degrade, it **parks the whole duty on the owner**, who is the only person who can replace it. 📊 **MEASURED s2608, four days before the trigger: `~/.goldrush/rotation-salt` is PRESENT — `65` bytes, mode `600`, mtime `2026-09-03T10:43:17Z` — and READABLE (`fs.accessSync(R_OK)` returns, not merely "the stat succeeded"; a fire runs as the owner's user, so mode 600 is not a barrier). The registry corroborates the schedule independently: `2` rotations, `r2026w38` `opensAt 2026-09-14` / `closesAt 2026-09-21`, so `r2026w39` opens **`2026-09-21T00:00:00.000Z`** and F-2568-1's "mint ON OR AFTER the Monday `opensAt`, never on the Sunday" resolves to that instant.** ⚖️ **SEVERITY STATED HONESTLY AND DELIBERATELY NOT INFLATED — THIS IS A NEGATIVE RESULT, NOT A DEFECT: nothing is missing, nothing is broken, no duty has ever failed on this, and the realised cost is ZERO. It is banked ONLY because F-2214-1 makes a negative result inherit a measurement's duties, and because the next reader would otherwise spend the check again or, worse, not spend it.** 🎯 **What earns it a row is the DIRECTION and the CLOCK: the salt is the one input to this duty that the factory does not own, cannot regenerate and must not default — so its absence is discoverable ONLY by looking, and the cheapest moment to look is BEFORE the trigger rather than at 00:00Z on a Monday when the answer is a desk line and a lost week. Checked four days early it costs one `stat`; checked on the day it costs the rotation.** ⓘ **WHAT THIS DOES *NOT* ESTABLISH, stated so it is not over-read: I did not run the mint, did not read the salt's CONTENT, and did not verify it is the same salt that produced `r2026w37`/`r2026w38` — a salt that is present but WRONG would mint seeds that verify against nothing, and that failure is invisible to this check by construction. The mtime (`2026-09-03`) predates both existing rotations, which is CONSISTENT with an unchanged salt but does not prove it.** 🚫 **NO GUARD, and the restraint is INHERITED rather than re-argued: the salt is deliberately outside the repo and is never committed, so a red keyed on it would fire on any machine that is not Robin's — and "did a fire pre-flight a dated duty?" is unobservable to every battery, the same reason F-1669-1 declined one for a filename read with the eyes, F-2391-1 and F-2562-2 for hand-typed date windows, F-2567-1 for a hand-typed clock and F-2599-1 for a `| tail`. The cure is this row, read at triage by the fire that inherits the trigger.** 💡 **REUSABLE, and it is F-2595-1's lesson turned one step earlier: that finding says type the VERBS rather than re-check the FACTS. The rung under it is that **a verb has PRECONDITIONS, and a precondition owned by someone outside the factory is the one that cannot be fixed in the moment.** When a dated duty is approaching, enumerate what its first command READS — not what it writes, and not what it asserts — and check that those inputs exist while there is still time for an owner to answer.

🧪 **F-2597-1 — AN ENUMERATION IN A LAW SURFACE CERTIFIES THE MEMBERS IT DID NOT COUNT: RT-01's "THREE other guard consumers" IS FOUR, AND THE UNCOUNTED ONE IS THE ONLY ONE THAT PINS A ROTATION ID AS A HARDCODED LITERAL (fire s2597, dry board, 65th consecutive).** ✅ **THE VERDICT FIRST, SO THE CORRECTION IS NOT MISREAD AS AN ALARM: the Monday `r2026w39` mint is SAFE, and that is MEASURED rather than argued — a scratch mint into a COPY of the registry (never the tracked file, 3 days before the trigger) leaves `rotations[0]` **BYTE-IDENTICAL**, so all four `rotations[0]` consumers are append-safe and a mint changes nothing for any of them.** 📊 **MEASURED s2597 by RE-SWEEPING the consumers instead of inheriting the list: `bench-seeds.test.mjs:124` · `review-party-retention.test.mjs:14` · `test-standings.mjs:1189` — the three the law names — **plus `e2e/transfer-board.spec.ts`, which it does not**, importing the registry at `:4` and keying on `rotations[0]` at `:20` and `:32`.** 🔑 **AND THE FOURTH IS QUALITATIVELY DIFFERENT, WHICH IS WHY IT IS THE ONE WORTH FINDING: at `:31` it asserts `toContainText('r2026w37 closes')` — a HARDCODED id literal, NOT derived from `rotations[0].id`. It agrees with its derived sibling at `:32` ONLY because the registry is APPEND-ONLY (`rotation-mint.mjs:52-53` filters the same id, concats, sorts by `opensAt`, so a new rotation always sorts LAST and `rotations[0]` is frozen). **That convention is load-bearing for a string literal and was written down nowhere.** The day anyone PRUNES the oldest rotation, `:31` breaks LOUD on a stale literal while `:32` SILENTLY FOLLOWS the new `rotations[0]` — one fails, one changes subject.** ⚖️ **SEVERITY STATED HONESTLY AND DELIBERATELY NOT INFLATED: realised cost ZERO, nothing is broken, NOT a false green, no mint was ever wrong, and nothing is owed before Monday. This corrects an ENUMERATION, not a verdict.** 🎯 **What earns it a row is WHO READS THE COUNT AND WHEN: that clause exists so a fire can budget a mint's blast radius, and it hands that fire a NUMBER — so a fire checking "the three consumers" stops at three and never opens the one file whose coupling is a literal. F-2358-1 exactly: *a guard enumerating one member of a class certifies the uncovered members as clean* — here it is a LAW enumerating three of four.** 🖨️ **A SECOND, USABLE FACT BANKED AT THE SITE: the fence body is **BYTE-IDENTICAL** to `JSON.stringify(registry, null, 2)` (30 lines, compared EQUAL and not merely `deepEqual`), so RT-01 step 2 is a REGENERATION, not a hand-paste — and hand-pasting 30 lines into 43 is precisely the step that can silently drop a rotation and re-create the defect F-2594-1 cured.** 🔢 **s2595's EXPLICIT RE-VERIFY INSTRUCTION IS DISCHARGED, AND STRUCTURALLY RATHER THAN BY LUCK: the SOLE law pointer into `public/skill.md` is `:367` (measured — 74 baseline sources, exactly one targets that file) and the fence spans `371–404`, so the pointer sits 4 lines ABOVE a block that grows DOWNWARD. Measured growth **+13 lines per rotation** (371–404 today → 371–417 after the mint). No law pointer rots on a mint; `0` baseline pointers target `scripts/fire.md` at all.** 📈 **ONE DATED, COMPOUNDING CONSEQUENCE NAMED SO IT IS NOT DISCOVERED LATE: +13 lines/week forever is ~700 lines of JSON a year on `public/skill.md`, a RIDER-FACING page. Nothing owed today — recorded because the trim that eventually follows is exactly the act that breaks `:31` above.** 🚫 **NO GUARD, and the restraint is INHERITED rather than re-argued: "does this prose still enumerate its class completely?" is a judgement over free text, so a red fires on every honest sentence and is excused into uselessness inside a week (F-1460-1, the `cross-engine` fate) — the same restraint F-2450-1 took for a live instruction and F-2595-1 took for this very duty. The cure is the amended clause in `scripts/fire.md`.** 💡 **REUSABLE, and it is the RUNG UNDER s2595's lesson: that finding said a dated duty accumulates verified FACTS and unverified VERBS, so TYPE THE STEPS.
